procedural_matters: POL19 was represented by Dominiki Busac. NED69 was represented by Michiel Dam.
The panel of the International Jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
facts: Race 1 of 49er Yellow, with 16 knots and flat seas.
POL 19 entered the zone of mark 4P on starboard tack 2 hull lengths below the port lay-line with IND one hull-length clear ahead of her.
At that moment, NED 69 was sailing on port tack towards mark 4P, 5 boat length away from it.
IND gybed and POL 19 luffed about 20º passing behind IND and turning on a collision course with NED 69.
NED 69 held her course, and when NED 69 entered the zone, a contact occurred between POL's bowsprit and the port side of the hull of NED 69.
POL 19 bowsprit broke in two pieces.
conclusions: NED 69 on port tack failed to keep clear of POL 19 on starboard tack, and broke RRS 10.
NED 69 outside overlapped at the zone failed to give POL 19 mark-room, and broke RRS 18.2(a)(1).
NED 69 did not avoid contact with POL 19 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).

It was not reasonably possible for POL 19 the right-of-way boat and the boat sailing within the room to which she was entitled to avoid contact with NED 69 when it became clear that NED 69 was not keeping clear and giving mark-room. POL 19 did not break RRS 14(a).

POL 19’s score in race 1 was made significantly worse through no fault of her own by physical damage because of the action of NED 69 that was breaking RRS 10 and RRS 18.2(a)(1) and was penalized. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(2) are met.
decision: NED 69 is DSQ in R1. Redress is given to POL 19. POL 19 is to be scored in race 1 points equal to the average, rounded to the nearest tenth of a point (0.05 to be rounded upward), of their points in all races sailed in the Preliminary series on Monday 30th and Tuesday 31st, except race 1. No other boat’s score shall change.
